placements.why: Nothing in the (empty) strata or graph structure holds technical/infrastructure decisions — this envelope's entire content is a database-technology switch, which is squarely an architecture-grain organizational category. Minting standalone since no existing category is even close; a strata mint needs no parent already in place.
placements.title: technical infrastructure and system-design decisions
placements.frame: What technology, system, or infrastructure choice is being made, and what does it commit the organization to build or replace?

placements.title: adopting new technology stacks on quantified performance-and-cost grounds
placements.frame: What quantified performance or cost advantage is being invoked to justify moving off an established technology, and what commitment (timeline, scope) is attached to that move?
placements.why: All five segments — the spoken announcement-plus-rationale (src-1, src-2) and the ratifying summary record (src-3, src-4, src-5) — carry one recurring thematic subject: a technology-stack switch justified by quantified performance/cost gains and bounded by a timeline. This is a pattern future envelopes on other migrations or decision records would keep feeding (the grain test), not a one-time fact — the '10x'/'lower licensing cost'/'Q3 2026' figures are evidence FOR this theme, not leaves of their own. No existing leaf covers it (graph structure is empty), and it is close enough in kind to the newly-minted Architecture strata to sit directly under it rather than stand fully alone.
